name: 211info
description: Free, confidential help line for Oregon and SW Washington. Connects people to current rent, utility, shelter, food, and other programs — including assistance funds that open and close throughout the year.
hours: Phone 24/7; text and chat hours vary

name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: Call, text, or chat 988 any time to talk with a trained crisis counselor about suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, or a mental health or substance use crisis. Press 3 or text PRIDE for LGBTQIA2S+ counselors where available.

name: National Runaway Safeline
description: Confidential support for young people who have run away, are thinking about it, or are homeless or in crisis. Can help with safe transportation home through Home Free and connect to local shelter.

name: The Trevor Project
description: Crisis counseling and suicide prevention for LGBTQIA2S+ young people, by phone, text, or chat. Also runs TrevorSpace, an online peer community.

name: Trans Lifeline
description: Peer support hotline run by and for trans people. Also offers microgrants for name changes and ID updates.

name: Oregon YouthLine
description: Teen-to-teen crisis and peer support line. Youth answer calls, texts, and chats in the afternoons/evenings, with adult counselors available at all other times.

name: Oregon Child Abuse Hotline
description: Report abuse or neglect of anyone under 18, including yourself. Trained screeners decide next steps to keep kids safe.

name: National Human Trafficking Hotline
description: Confidential help for anyone being forced or pressured into sex, work, or other acts — or anyone worried someone else is.

name: Call to Safety
description: 24-hour crisis line for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and dating violence in the Portland area. Can help with safety planning and connecting to confidential shelter.

name: Multnomah County Behavioral Health Crisis Line
description: Local 24/7 mental health crisis line. Can send a mobile crisis team in some situations.

name: Washington County Crisis Line
description: Local 24/7 mental health crisis line for Washington County residents.

name: Clackamas County Crisis Line
description: Local 24/7 mental health crisis line for Clackamas County residents.

name: Janus Youth Programs — Youth Crisis Shelter & Homeless Youth Services
description: Runs emergency shelter and crisis services for children and teens, plus programs in Multnomah County's Homeless Youth Continuum for older youth (outreach, shelter, and transitional housing). Call or check the website for which program fits your age.

name: Janus Youth Programs — Vancouver Youth Shelter
description: Emergency shelter and crisis support for youth under 18 in Clark County, with family reunification support when safe.

name: Outside In
description: Downtown Portland drop-in for youth experiencing homelessness: meals, showers, laundry, case management, housing programs, education and job support, plus a medical clinic (including gender-affirming care) open to the community.

name: New Avenues for Youth
description: Drop-in, housing, education, and job training programs for youth experiencing or at risk of homelessness, including paid job training through youth-run social enterprises and support for youth who have experienced exploitation.

name: p:ear
description: Mentoring through art, education, recreation, and job training for youth experiencing homelessness. Drop-in space, art studio, and paid internships.

name: Native American Youth and Family Center (NAYA)
description: Culturally specific services for Native youth and families: youth programs and an early college academy, housing and homeless services, rent and energy assistance, and workforce programs.

name: Urban League of Portland
description: Culturally specific services centering Black Oregonians, including housing support, rent assistance (when funded), and workforce training and job placement.

name: Latino Network
description: Culturally specific youth and family programs for Latine communities, including school-based youth support, mentoring, and family stabilization services.

name: El Programa Hispano Católico
description: Bilingual services in East Multnomah County including energy bill assistance, rent assistance, and youth programs. Spanish speakers welcome.
eligibility: Utility and rent assistance usually require being the adult named on the bill or lease and meeting income limits.

name: IRCO (Immigrant and Refugee Community Organization)
description: Services for immigrant and refugee youth and families in many languages: youth programs, school support, employment, and energy bill assistance.

name: Multnomah County Energy Assistance
description: Helps low-income households pay heating and electric bills (LIHEAP/OEAP) and avoid shutoff. Applications go through community partner agencies when funding is open.
eligibility: You must be the person (or in the household) responsible for the bill, and meet income limits.

name: Home Forward
description: Multnomah County's housing authority: affordable apartments, Housing Choice Vouchers, and Foster Youth to Independence (FYI) vouchers for young adults leaving foster care. Waitlists open periodically.

name: Community Action (Washington County)
description: Washington County's community action agency: energy bill assistance, rent and eviction-prevention help, housing support, and Head Start for families with young children.

name: HomePlate Youth Services
description: Drop-in nights, meals, supplies, case management, and housing navigation for youth experiencing housing instability in Washington County.

name: Boys & Girls Aid
description: Safe Place youth shelter for teens who can't stay at home, plus transitional housing and support for young people leaving foster care.

name: Clackamas County Social Services
description: Energy bill assistance, rent assistance and eviction prevention, and housing help for Clackamas County residents.

name: Northwest Housing Alternatives
description: Affordable housing and homeless services in Clackamas County, including the Annie Ross House family shelter and rent assistance programs.

name: Council for the Homeless — Housing Solutions Center
description: Clark County's front door for shelter, housing, and rent help. Call the Housing Solutions Center to be screened for shelter and housing programs.

name: Vancouver Housing Authority
description: Clark County's housing authority: affordable housing and vouchers, including Foster Youth to Independence (FYI) vouchers.

name: Clark Public Utilities — Bill Assistance
description: Payment plans and bill assistance programs for Clark Public Utilities customers having trouble paying electric or water bills.

name: PGE Income-Qualified Bill Discount
description: Monthly discount on PGE electric bills for income-qualified customers, plus payment arrangements to avoid disconnection.
eligibility: For PGE customers whose name is on the account and who meet income limits.

name: Pacific Power Low-Income Bill Discount
description: Bill discount for income-qualified Pacific Power customers in Oregon, plus payment plans.

name: NW Natural Bill Discount & Assistance
description: Bill discount and assistance for income-qualified natural gas customers in Oregon and SW Washington.

name: Oregon Energy Fund
description: Nonprofit that helps Oregon households pay energy bills, working through local partner agencies.

name: Portland Water Bureau — Financial Assistance
description: Discounts, crisis vouchers, and payment plans for Portland sewer, stormwater, and water bills.

name: Yamhill Community Action Partnership (YCAP)
description: Energy bill assistance, rent help, housing and shelter navigation, food, and youth outreach in Yamhill County.

name: Community Action Team (Columbia County)
description: Energy bill assistance, rent help, housing programs, and Head Start serving Columbia County.

name: Independent Living Program (ILP) & Chafee Housing
description: For current and former foster youth: life skills, help with education and jobs, and Chafee housing funds to help pay rent while transitioning to adulthood. Ask your caseworker or contact ODHS.
eligibility: Eligibility depends on time spent in foster care; ages vary by service.

name: Bridge Meadows
description: Intergenerational housing communities for families adopting youth from foster care, elders, and young adults who have aged out of foster care.

name: Youth Villages — LifeSet
description: Intensive one-on-one support for young adults transitioning out of foster care or the justice system: housing, school, work, and relationships.

name: PCC Future Connect
description: College success program for first-generation and low-income students: scholarships, advising, and support starting in the first year at PCC.

name: POIC + Rosemary Anderson High School
description: Alternative high school, re-engagement, mentoring, and job training for youth who have been pushed out of or left traditional school.

name: Portland YouthBuilders
description: Earn a high school diploma or GED while training in construction or technology, with stipends, case management, and job placement.

name: Job Corps
description: Free career training and education. Most students live on campus with housing, meals, and healthcare included while they train.

name: WorkSource Oregon / Worksystems Youth Programs
description: Job search help, paid work experience, and training funds. Ask about youth employment programs for ages 16–24.

name: Oregon Food Bank — Find Food
description: Map of free food pantries and meal sites across Oregon and Clark County. No ID required at most pantries.

name: WIC (Women, Infants & Children)
description: Free healthy food, breastfeeding support, and nutrition help for people who are pregnant or parenting children under 5. Teens qualify on their own.

name: Multnomah County Student Health Centers
description: Free, confidential medical and mental health care at school-based clinics for any young person in the county, insured or not. Youth 15+ can consent to their own care in Oregon.

name: Q Center
description: Portland's LGBTQIA2S+ community center: youth and young adult groups, peer support, and resource referrals.

name: Raphael House of Portland
description: Confidential emergency shelter, advocacy, and housing support for survivors of domestic violence and their children.

name: Domestic Violence Resource Center
description: Washington County crisis line, emergency shelter, and advocacy for survivors of domestic and dating violence.

name: Clackamas Women's Services
description: Support for survivors of domestic and sexual violence, trafficking, and stalking in Clackamas County, including shelter and youth-specific advocacy. Serves all genders.

name: YWCA Clark County — SafeChoice
description: Confidential shelter, advocacy, and support for survivors of domestic and sexual violence in Clark County.

name: Safety Compass
description: Advocacy for survivors of commercial sexual exploitation and trafficking, including youth, in the Portland metro area.

name: Youth, Rights & Justice
description: Legal representation and advocacy for youth in the juvenile justice and child welfare systems, plus help with school discipline and expungement.

name: Legal Aid Services of Oregon / Oregon Law Center
description: Free civil legal help for low-income Oregonians, including eviction defense, benefits, and family law. OregonLawHelp.org has self-help guides.

name: Community Alliance of Tenants — Renters' Rights Hotline
description: Renter education and hotline for Oregon tenants facing eviction, repairs, or landlord problems.

name: TriMet Youth & Low-Income Fares
description: Reduced fares for youth 7–17 and income-qualified adults (Honored Citizen). Many Portland-area high school students can get a free pass through their school.

name: Lifeline Phone & Internet Discount
description: Federal program that lowers the cost of phone or internet service for people on SNAP, Medicaid/OHP, SSI, or with low income. Oregon adds its own discount.

name: Oregon SNAP, OHP & Cash Assistance (ONE)
description: Apply in one place for SNAP food benefits, Oregon Health Plan (free health coverage), TANF, and childcare help (ERDC).

name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
description: Free, confidential support for anyone experiencing abuse in a relationship or at home — safety planning, someone to talk to, and connections to local shelter and advocates.

name: love is respect
description: Dating abuse help line built for teens and young adults. Talk, text, or chat about a relationship that doesn't feel right — for yourself or a friend.

name: StrongHearts Native Helpline
description: Culturally grounded, confidential support for Native people affected by domestic, dating, and sexual violence, staffed by Native advocates.

name: RAINN National Sexual Assault Hotline
description: Confidential support after sexual assault or abuse, any time it happened. Connects you to a local sexual assault service provider.

name: Bradley Angle
description: Portland domestic violence services: confidential emergency shelter, housing support, and support groups, with programs specifically for LGBTQIA2S+ survivors and Black and African American survivors.
eligibility: Ages served vary by program — ask about youth eligibility.

name: Henderson House
description: Crisis line, confidential shelter, and advocacy for survivors of domestic and sexual violence in Yamhill County.

name: Central City Concern
description: Portland nonprofit offering recovery-focused housing, an employment center, health care, and peer support — including services for people leaving jail or prison.

name: Bridges to Change
description: Peer mentors with lived experience plus transitional and recovery housing for people coming out of incarceration or in recovery.

name: Constructing Hope
description: Paid-pathway pre-apprenticeship construction training that welcomes people with conviction histories and centers people of color.

name: Oregon Youth Authority — Transition & Parole Services
description: For youth in or leaving OYA custody: transition planning, housing and school/work support, and help connecting to community services. Ask your parole/probation officer or OYA staff.

name: Metropolitan Public Defender — Record Clearing
description: Free help clearing (expunging/setting aside) eligible criminal records so they don't block housing, jobs, or school.

name: Multnomah County Department of Community Justice
description: Juvenile and adult community justice services, including reentry and transition support, housing and treatment referrals for people on supervision.

name: Self Enhancement, Inc. (SEI)
description: Culturally specific services centering Black youth and families in Portland: school-based mentoring, after-school programs, and housing stabilization including rent and energy assistance when funded.

name: Black Parent Initiative
description: Support for Black and multiracial parents and caregivers: parenting education, home visiting, and family support.

name: APANO (Asian Pacific American Network of Oregon)
description: Asian and Pacific Islander community organization with youth leadership programs, community resources, and referrals in many languages.

name: Centro Cultural de Washington County
description: Latine-led community center in Cornelius serving Washington County with workforce training, youth programs, and family support including help with basic needs and bills when funded.

name: Bienestar
description: Affordable housing and resident services for Latine and immigrant families in Washington County.

name: Adelante Mujeres
description: Education and empowerment programs for Latina women and youth in Washington County, including youth leadership and school support.

name: NARA Northwest
description: Culturally specific health care, mental health, and addiction treatment and recovery services for Native people and the wider community, including youth programs.

name: Planned Parenthood Columbia Willamette
description: Confidential sexual and reproductive health care: birth control, STI testing, pregnancy testing and options, and gender-affirming care. Teens can get many services without a parent.
